vulnerability_mechanism.detail: The authoritative repository advisory and local source agree: raw getattr/setattr/hasattr are exposed in safe_builtins, RestrictedPython execution has no _getattr_ guard, the merge lets project builtins override RestrictedPython builtins, and validate_code only detects literal dangerous dunder substrings. Runtime-built attribute names therefore reach class-hierarchy traversal and subprocess.Popen.

atomic_bic.detail: cb5cd12a5882b59a8e441e84e636b2b960dc912f is a public, single-parent PR member that adds server_fastmcp.py as a new 677-line file with the complete vulnerable mechanism. The advisory's f855e54d5b7bc1c91b977574a03b91eff6b86bb6 is an unrelated later migration commit, not the BIC.

immediate_parent_absence.detail: The BIC's immediate parent is 7af39689f6d99b6659f064bd7bba78b7025279e1. That parent has no server_fastmcp.py at the sandbox path and no matching python_sandbox/RestrictedPython safe-builtin mechanism.

squash_member_decomposition.detail: The nine public members form a linear chain from cb5cd12a5882b59a8e441e84e636b2b960dc912f through b224d445611b2998d0f9ac45ad9f990350a4a43c. Only the first member creates the mechanism; later members format, document, chmod, or add headers. b224d445611b2998d0f9ac45ad9f990350a4a43c has the same tree as alternate squash landing d2333551cd5907b56cfcdd2a244e095ab72512e4, while mainline landing 771ffb8ebc0b8f97cce470dbc7cbf41f5d12747b carries the same sandbox blob on a different base.

affected_and_fixed_release_membership.detail: Primary release evidence is wrong about v0.9.0, v1.0.0-BETA-1, and v1.0.0-RC1. Each contains alternate landing d2333551cd5907b56cfcdd2a244e095ab72512e4 and the vulnerable raw getattr/setattr plus merged_builtins.update(our_builtins). v1.0.1 is likewise vulnerable. Fix 63a2900e6301b9c8a483a38d3737a1beb3a7ce89 is absent from v1.0.1 and an ancestor of v1.0.2; v1.0.2 removes the raw builtins and installs _guarded_getattr as _getattr_.

direct_fix_or_verified_unpatched.detail: 63a2900e6301b9c8a483a38d3737a1beb3a7ce89 directly removes raw getattr/setattr/hasattr, reverses the builtins merge precedence, installs _getattr_/_setattr_ guards, replaces substring checking with AST inspection, fails closed without RestrictedPython, and requires bearer authentication for HTTP.

bic_only_ai_attribution.detail: The BIC object names Mihai Criveti as author and committer and contains only a matching Signed-off-by trailer. It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other explicit AI marker. Those facts are BIC-local, but absence of an AI marker and a human-looking identity do not independently prove that the vulnerable code was human-written, so NOT_AI is not closed.

findings: The atomic introducer, parent absence, squash/member lineage, mechanism, direct fix, and v1.0.2 fix boundary independently reproduce.

The primary record incorrectly excludes v0.9.0, v1.0.0-BETA-1, and v1.0.0-RC1 by following only landing 771ffb8ebc0b8f97cce470dbc7cbf41f5d12747b; those tags contain the equivalent d2333551cd5907b56cfcdd2a244e095ab72512e4 landing and remain vulnerable.
The primary NOT_AI conclusion relies on absent commit markers plus a human identity. That is insufficient causal authorship evidence under the BIC-only fail-closed gate.

corrected_fields.ai_marker: No explicit AI marker is present on BIC cb5cd12a5882b59a8e441e84e636b2b960dc912f; this absence does not establish human-only authorship.

remaining_gap: BIC-only evidence does not establish whether cb5cd12a5882b59a8e441e84e636b2b960dc912f's vulnerable code was authored with or without AI assistance; absent explicit commit markers cannot close NOT_AI.
